simple.meaning: קְשִׂיטָה (qᵉsîyṭâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “an ingot (as definitely estimated and stamped for a coin).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 33:19. The surrounding context includes family, family line, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְשִׂיטָה (H7192) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

majorEvents.label: Genealogy
majorEvents.evidenceText: They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver.† Hebrew: kesitahs. A kesitah was a kind of silver coin. They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

timeline.evidenceText: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.

They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver.† Hebrew: kesitahs. A kesitah was a kind of silver coin. They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money,* literally, kesitah, a unit of money, probably silver and everyone a ring of gold.
